newsitem.title: USA: US refiners pocket mix of foreign crude for August.
newsitem.headline: US refiners pocket mix of foreign crude for August.

text.p: U.S. refiners pocketed a mix of foreign crudes for August runs in recent days, although activity tapered off on Friday afternoon ahead of this weekend's crucial U.N.-Iraqi meeting in Baghdad, traders said.
Norwegian Statoil on Friday placed the last of five Brent cargoes off a ULCC arriving July 15-20 with a Gulf Coast refiner, traders said.
The cargo was heard sold at August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus 25-30 cents a barrel.
On Thursday, the same company sold two half cargoes of 250,000 barrels each of Norwegian Oseberg to two Gulf Coast refiners at 40-50 cents under WTI/Cushing for end-July delivery, traders said.
From Latin America, equity producer Total on Thursday sold a Colombian Cusiana cargo to a U.S. refiner at October WTI minus 85-90 cents a barrel fob, traders said.

An East Coast refiner was heard to be reselling Cusiana crude for July 27-28 loading. The firm holds two Cusiana cargoes for that time frame that it picked up from Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol, paying around $1.35 under WTI.
Elsewhere in Latin America, Venezuelan Mesa-30 crude was pegged around $2.90-3.10 a barrel under WTI, while Leona crude was assessed around $4.40 a barrel under WTI.

On the Asian front, privately held Koch Oil on July 9 sold a Malaysian combination cargo of 550,000 barrels of Tapis and 470,000 barrels of Labuan to a Houston refiner for delivery at the end of August.
The Tapis was placed at six cents over October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing on a delivered basis, while the Labuan fetched parity to October WTI, traders said.
Separately, Swiss trader Vitol on July 10 sold an Indonesian Widuri cargo to a U.S. refiner for delivery around August 20 at about $1.35 under WTI, traders said.

Buying eased off on Friday afternoon as traders awaited this Sunday's meeting between the U.N. humanitarian coordinator in Iraq, Staffan de Mistura, and Iraqi officials concerning Baghadad's aid distribution plan.
U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan must approve the plan in order to restart oil exports under the oil-for-food program.
